status: completed
id: 998854ff-c48e-4d59-ba6b-7521fee1fa10
terrain: Continuous natural gray and taupe stone ground at the mountain foot, subdued weathered bedrock surface, flat lower terrain beneath a substantial cliff, crisp original pixel art. No loose decorative rocks, boulder sprites, bushes, trees, grass, roads or masonry walls. -> Elevated continuous rocky mountain terrace of pale weathered gray and taupe stone, broad light stone upper surface with natural cracks, jagged slab cap along the terrace rim. A continuous rectangular game world, not a floating island or isolated diorama. No grass, bushes, trees, decorative rocks, buildings or roads.
tiles: 25
tile_size: 32x32px
transition tileset: spritesheet is a 4x8 grid (not 4x4); cliff-wall tiles have 'transition' corners and fill the map cell BELOW the terrain boundary, so a cliff spans two rows. Select tiles via pattern_4x4 in the metadata (row_0/row_3 = terrain above/below), not corners alone.
view: low top-down
style: selective outline, detailed shading, highly detailed
transition: Deep continuous natural cliff faces joining the elevated rocky terrace to the lower stone ground at the mountain foot. Substantial dark exposed gray rock faces with strong vertical fractures, irregular layered slabs and jagged pale stone caps; strong dark shadow beneath the overhanging cap and along the cliff foot. Joined cliff walls must continue seamlessly across adjacent straight tiles, inside and outside corners and wall-continuation tiles. Natural mountain escarpment, not separate boulder sprites, stacked decorative rocks, a road retaining wall, brickwork or a floating diorama. Pale weathered upper surface contrasting with dark vertically fractured gray faces, muted gray/taupe palette, crisp pixel clusters.

placement: pick each tile by its corners (NW/NE/SW/SE) or pattern_4x4, then slice the sheet with that tile's `bounding_box` from the metadata â it is the exact rect, and it is correct for BOTH the 16-tile sheet and the 25-tile transition sheet. The metadata endpoint computes bounding_box when serving (it is not a stored column, so querying the database for it finds nothing) and strips each tile's `image` object, so there is no per-tile URL to fetch. Two things are NOT sheet positions: the `wang_N` NAME, and `original_position` (the generation grid â its row can exceed this sheet). Using either is what produces horizontal banding.
